title: Sulawesi cave art (Maros-Pangkep karst)
summary: The limestone caves of the Maros-Pangkep karst in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, hold some of the oldest dated figurative paintings. At Leang Karampuang a panel of three human-like figures and a wild pig was dated, by uranium-series analysis of mineral crusts over it, to at least 51,200 years ago; a hunting scene at Leang Bulu' Sipong 4 was re-dated to about 48,000 years.

uncertainty.note: Minimum age: "at least 51,200 years ago" (Griffith) and a minimum age of 51.2 ka (53.5 ± 2.3 ka) (Nature paper). Year = 1950 minus 51,200; the painting is older. The sources give Leang Bulu' Sipong 4 as about 48,000 years (main text) and 50.2 ± 2.2 ka (abstract) inconsistently.

as_recorded.value: a minimum age of 51.2 ka (53.5 ± 2.3 ka)

reviewer_note: Dates are minimum ages. The pin is the centre of Maros Regency, not a cave; the article gives no coordinates and the karst spans Maros and Pangkep. Leang Bulu' Sipong 4 is given as about 48,000 years in the main text and 50.2 ka in the abstract, so the summary uses the Griffith figure. Leang Tedongnge (45.5 ka) is left out because it was seen only in search snippets.
